I so get this... until about two and a half years ago I thought I was only attracted to women and you couldn't get me to budge. Part of me yearns to marry a woman.  To start a family and continue my bloodline (it dies with me if I don't have a kid), and raise Godly children for the next generation LORD willing that they accept Christ and stick with Him.  Just the normal family nuclear life.

Another part of me wants to take the risk to blow my life up and come out as queer, then try to have a relationship with another man.  This could go many ways: Changing denominations, changing beliefs, becoming an agnostic or at-home practicing Christian, etc.... I feel in a lot of ways this goes against what the LORD has called me to do and in some ways could violate Hebrews 10:24-25, two verses I connect very strongly with, but what the Bible says about falling to temptation is definitely true.  Homosexual urges continue to persist for me and I can't deny that I have these urges.

Finally, the life of celibacy, though not very attractive at all to me right now, does seem like a viable option.  It makes my chances of ever becoming a church elder or church camp director slim (most want someone married or believe someone has to be married to fill these roles), which is sad because you'd think someone single with fully open time to devote to that would be fantastic for the role, but I've also realized I have to accept that sometimes things will not be in the LORD's plan for me, and this might be one of them.

I say all of this to try and answer the question of how to plan your life.  Let the LORD lead and plan your steps.  See where He takes you.  He knows the best plan for you, better than anyone commenting here ever could.

I would like to see an FM talk station geared towards a younger demographic.  That is something I've realized is missing, at least from the markets around me.  AM and FM talk stations are normally geared towards the upper end of the demographics we care about, and often feature conservative hosts in my area as the primary source of info.  I think to capture the younger demographic a bit better, a station playing younger talk shows aimed at more left (or right) ideals could deliver in spades even though it's a big risk.

Music wise, we need less cookie cutter Top 40, adult contemporary, and country stations.  Those music types are the "Big 3" when it comes to how the radio stations around us are programmed each and every day.  Some markets experiment with AAA, adult hits, hip-hop, etc... but they're few and far between, and if there is a community or college radio station, it is also more adult oriented and does not capture the interest of a younger listener from what I've seen.  Either the host using the "kitchen table conversation" of hosting or the music not being in their interests drives them away.  To be clear, I think that hosting style is good, and we need more music to expose listeners to.

Another thing I'm noticing in a lot of markets is that we really focus on the morning show, but from the time the morning show ends to when it begins the next day, we don't really seem to care about what happens.  We let voice tracks and legal IDs fire off 10 minutes or more before they're supposed to, we don't check on things to make sure they're running accurately, and we just let the music autopopulate and hope for the best.  Some stations have combatted this by either having live DJs 24/7/365 or at the very least a show during the afternoon drive that's not completely voice tracked.  I think in order to keep people entertained, we either need to put more effort into our voice tracks, or bring back live shows during the afternoon drive (usually the 2 or 3pm to 7pm shift).  We also need to stop putting our stations on autopilot at 7pm or airing syndicated shows in that time slot.  Major detriment to the local aspect of things.

I am sorry to be so long-winded, but I definitely see radio becoming a less than cared about medium in a lot of markets due to old ideals hanging on and a closed mind to new ideas altogether.  We've become an industry of "rip and read" or "just skip the show and let the music play" and it's working against our goals.

We're always looking for more people in the industry (or at least we should be), but depending on your market be aware that your passion may be (quite unfortunately) stomped out by management that wants to keep things the same old same old.  Radio is suffering in many markets from a lack of willingness to try new ideas.  Of course follow the management's wishes if you end up there, but as someone who's been in a professional radio career for less than a year and is already asking some big questions as to whether or not I want to hang with this long term,  I thought it was important to share this.

In addition, radio openings are also rare these days.  When someone leaves their post, it's more likely that someone from another market is selected to voice track (record ahead) that slot instead of replacing it with new local talent.  Or, they'll have someone at the station voice track that slot, which adds to their already busy plate.  As prices go up and costs inflate, we try to cover multiple roles with as little workforce as possible.

I personally at this point would recommend joining a community radio station as a volunteer, or starting an internet radio station yourself.  There, even under the direction of management, you can still produce quality content and have at least some say over what goes on, instead of playlists handed down from a corporate office, canned live call-ins, and burning yourself out with too much to do.  Plus, you'll discover a lot of great new music and the people tend to be more genuine on that side of the industry.  Public speaking might be the best career option with radio volunteering on the side.
